title: The Holiday Supplement on the Nightly Resort Charge, Resort Lodging
content:
A holiday supplement is added to the nightly charge for the nights of a Resort Lodging stay being charged, and how much is added turns on how the nights the reservation covers sit against the unit type's published holiday window. That window runs from the 19th of December 2026 to the 2nd of January 2027 inclusive.

Where every night the reservation covers falls inside the unit type's published holiday window, the holiday share of the nightly charge, being 25 percent of it, is added to it for each night charged.

Where some but not all of the nights the reservation covers fall inside that window, the half holiday share of the nightly charge, being 12.5 percent of it, is added to it for each night charged, which is how a stay spanning the turn of the window is blended.

Where no night the reservation covers falls inside that window, nothing is added.

| How the nights the reservation covers sit against the holiday window | Added to the nightly charge for each night charged |
| --- | --- |
| Every night inside the window | 25 percent of the nightly charge |
| Some but not all inside the window | 12.5 percent of the nightly charge |
| No night inside the window | nothing |

### Three hypothetical reservations, where the nightly charge is taken here as 40.00 USD

A reservation covering the nights of the 22nd to the 27th of December 2026 has every night inside the holiday window, so 10.00 USD is added to the nightly charge for each night charged, being 25 percent of 40.00 USD.

A reservation covering the nights of the 29th of December 2026 to the 4th of January 2027 has some of its nights inside the window and some after it, so 5.00 USD is added for each night charged, being 12.5 percent of 40.00 USD.

A reservation covering the nights of the 10th to the 14th of February 2027 has no night inside the holiday window, and nothing is added. It is the nights the reservation covers that are read against the window, not only the nights being charged.
